record.title: UK Data Centre Covenant links strategic support to energy, community, environmental and security tests
record.summary: HM Treasury published a Data Centre Covenant on 28 October 2026. All data centres are encouraged to meet its tests; projects designated strategic must meet them when seeking enhanced government support. The tests cover energy-system costs and flexibility, local-benefit plans, efficient energy and water use, annual reporting for strategic sites, UK jobs and supply chains, and secure compute. New facilities are expected to achieve PUE of 1.3 or better. In return, government describes faster or reallocated grid connections and a tightly controlled route to temporary on-site generation for exceptionally strategic projects when other routes cannot provide capacity in time. The government estimates the UK will need 6 GW of AI data-centre capacity by 2030. These are policy terms and a government estimate, not evidence of implementation, capacity delivered or measured outcomes.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: HM Treasury published the Data Centre Covenant on 28 October 2026.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The Covenant says data centres are encouraged to meet its tests and strategic data centres must meet them when seeking enhanced government support. It covers energy-system costs and grid flexibility, local-benefit plans, energy and water efficiency, annual resource reporting, UK jobs and supply chains, and security. New facilities are expected to achieve PUE of 1.3 or better.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The Covenant states the government estimates the UK will need 6 GW of AI data-centre capacity by 2030.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In return for meeting the tests, the government says it will consider support for strategic sites through faster or reallocated grid connections and, for exceptionally strategic projects under tightly controlled conditions, temporary on-site generation.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The publication does not establish which projects will qualify for enhanced support, whether the planned grid and energy measures will be delivered, whether facilities will comply, or whether the policy will reduce household costs or improve energy, water, emissions, security or community outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: The definition of a strategic data centre and additional project criteria are pending, and the practical verification/enforcement route for several Covenant expectations is not stated.

No project-level baseline or measurements establish actual connection acceleration, energy/water/emissions performance, household cost allocation, local-benefit delivery or effects on secure UK AI capacity.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented, conditioning enhanced government support and scarce grid access on energy, local-benefit, resource and security commitments could materially change the economics and operating requirements for strategic AI data-centre projects in the UK. The scope is nationally important but prospective; the document supplies no implementation or measured-outcome evidence.
limitations: The Covenant and Budget establish policy text and government plans, not project-level designation, approvals, grid connections, temporary-power grants, or facility compliance.
The definition of strategic data centres and additional criteria remain to be published; the meaning and enforcement of several expected commitments are not yet clear.
The 6 GW figure is a government estimate, not an independently assessed forecast or evidence that capacity has been contracted or built.
No facility-level energy, water, emissions, heat reuse, flexibility, household cost, security or local-benefit outcomes are reported.
brief.summary: HM Treasury published a Data Centre Covenant on 28 October 2026. All data centres are encouraged to meet its tests; projects designated strategic must meet them when seeking enhanced government support. The tests cover energy-system costs and flexibility, local-benefit plans, efficient energy and water use, annual reporting for strategic sites, UK jobs and supply chains, and secure compute. New facilities are expected to achieve PUE of 1.3 or better. In return, government describes faster or reallocated grid connections and a tightly controlled route to temporary on-site generation for exceptionally strategic projects when other routes cannot provide capacity in time. The government estimates the UK will need 6 GW of AI data-centre capacity by 2030. These are policy terms and a government estimate, not evidence of implementation, capacity delivered or measured outcomes.

technical.claimed_result: The government says the Covenant will support delivery of domestic data-centre capacity while securing energy-system, local, environmental, employment, supply-chain and security benefits. It estimates that 6 GW of AI data-centre capacity will be needed in the UK by 2030.
technical.demonstrated_result: HM Treasury published the Covenant and its stated policy design. No project-level authorization, connection acceleration, facility compliance or outcome is demonstrated.
technical.mechanism: The Covenant encourages all operators to meet a set of five tests and conditions enhanced government action for strategic sites on meeting those tests. It pairs energy-system commitments, local-benefit plans, resource-efficiency/reporting expectations, jobs and supply-chain commitments, and security cooperation with government action intended to accelerate power connections. Temporary on-site generation is reserved for exceptionally strategic projects where other measures cannot secure capacity in time and subject to conditions such as energy security.
technical.regime: UK data-centre projects, with additional tests tied to strategic designation and requests for enhanced government support; policy published 28 October 2026.
technical.reproducibility: Not applicable to the policy publication. Compliance and effects require project-level evidence and later evaluation.
technical.strongest_baseline: The policy document provides no baseline for data-centre energy/water use, grid connection waiting times, household cost allocation, local benefits, or domestic AI capacity against which effects can be evaluated.

brief.title: UK Data Centre Covenant links strategic support to energy, community, environmental and security tests
brief.why_it_matters: The Covenant connects the expansion of AI infrastructure with energy-system costs, local benefits, resource reporting, security and access to government support and power connections. If applied as described, it could affect data-centre project economics and the allocation and timing of UK grid capacity. The definition of strategic sites and additional criteria remain pending, and the document reports no project-level compliance or outcome evidence.
